text: 🇲🇽🛢️ Pemex and Petrobras: South-South energy sovereignty, signed this month. Sheinbaum confirmed the cooperation agreement between Mexico's Pemex and Brazil's Petrobras will be signed in June — covering deep-water and shallow-water exploration, with Brazilian technology transferred to revive Mexican production. "Brazilian technology is among the most advanced in the world. Petrobras has developed mechanisms that let us identify deeper reserves and re-analyze already-exploited fields." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on the Pemex–Petrobras pact Two state-owned oil companies, two governments that won't privatize their subsoil. The energy alternative to Washington isn't theoretical — it's a signature away.

🔥🇲🇽 "Bringing a Spanish deputy to lecture us about sovereignty is Kafkaesque." Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo — deputy from Spain's far-right Partido Popular — flew to Mexico for a Grupo Salinas event and declared that neither Hernán Cortés nor Isabella the Catholic ever violated Mexican sovereignty. Sheinbaum, at the podium: "They brought in another Spanish deputy — apparently these are the new cadres of Mexican politics. Having to import her to talk about national sovereignty is a bit Kafkaesque." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on the Mexican right's foreign imports

🇲🇽🌎 "Mexico's affairs are for Mexicans to decide." After US Ambassador Ronald Johnson publicly told the Mexican government to take "politics" out of the cartel fight, Sheinbaum drew the line at the podium. "Ambassadors must be respectful of the internal political affairs of countries. Our ambassador in the United States, in France, or anywhere in the world does not opine on the political affairs of those countries." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on Ronald Johnson Mexico's Constitution enshrines self-determination and non-intervention. Cooperation, yes — instructions from foreign envoys, no.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>WHILE MOODY'S DOWNGRADES, SPAIN SENDS 65 COMPANIES TO MEXICO TO DOUBLE DOWN</u>

Spanish Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo arrived in Mexico City with a 65-company delegation to sign a roadmap covering energy transition, infrastructure, financial services, digitalization, and tech innovation. Spain holds €68.8 billion in Mexico — the #2 FDI source after the US — with ~6,000 Spanish firms operating across banking, energy, telecom, tourism, and manufacturing. Per CamesCom: nearly 3 in 4 Spanish firms plan revenue growth in Mexico in 2026; over half plan to increase investment and headcount. Capital votes with its feet, not with the ratings agencies.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>CANADIAN HOTEL CHAIN ABANDONS CUBA UNDER US SANCTIONS PRESSURE — 15 PROPERTIES GONE</u>

Blue Diamond — Cuba's third-largest foreign hotel operator with 15 properties under Royalton, Memories, Starfish, Mystique, and Resonance brands across Havana, Varadero, and Cayo Largo — announced immediate exit June 1, hours before a US deadline forcing foreign firms to cut ties with companies "linked to Cuban Armed Forces." French CMA CGM and German Hapag-Lloyd already pulled shipping. Havana now living through 22-hour daily blackouts. The siege keeps tightening. Spanish Meliá and Iberostar (53 hotels combined) haven't moved — yet.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>BRUGADA: WORLD CUP MEXICO IS FOR THE PEOPLE WHO LIVE HERE — NOT JUST TOURISTS</u>

"Vivir el Mundial no solo es al interior del estadio, sino fuera de él," said CDMX Mayor Clara Brugada. The city will run special Metrobús, Trolebús, and Tren Ligero routes to the Estadio Azteca from north, central, and south zones — public transit prioritized over cars, free cultural events around the stadium for non-ticketed residents. Schools close June 11 for Mexico vs South Africa. FIFA's price-gouging machine meets the 4T's right-to-the-city framework.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>FOX-ERA CASINO TRIED TO DODGE 4.3 BILLION PESOS WITH A FORGED LOAN CONTRACT</u>

SHCP filed a 4,306,799,683 peso tax evasion case against Juegos del Bajío — a casino chain that got its permit under Vicente Fox with Santiago Creel as Gobernación. Notary Public No. 25 in Quintana Roo confirmed the company's 2019 loan contract was never protocolized; the witnesses to the notarization never existed. The Tribunal Administrativo nullified the fiscal credit anyway based on the fraudulent paper. Supreme Court reviews June 4. Minister Yasmín Esquivel still opposing review.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX-PETROBRAS DEEP WATER DEAL SIGNS THIS MONTH — SHEINBAUM CONFIRMS</u>

Pemex will sign a cooperation agreement with Petrobras in June for deep-water exploration, Sheinbaum confirmed today. Petrobras is "the most advanced company in the world" in deep-water extraction — the deal also covers mature fields like Cantarell. South-South energy sovereignty, no Big Oil intermediary. The model AMLO pointed toward, now operational.
